summary: Tested backend API endpoints (12/12 passing) and performed code review. Frontend is loading (HTTP 200) but browser automation (Playwright) is crashing with SIGSEGV in the headless Chromium shell - UI test coverage was not possible via automation. Frontend code review done manually from source.
action_items: Browser automation (Playwright) is crashing with SIGSEGV - frontend UI tests could not be executed. Manual code review confirms UI structure is correct per App.js.
critical_code_review_comments: RULE_PATTERN uses [$rule] regex but problem statement says [$rule_instruction] - regex is r'\[\$([^\]]+)\]' which matches [$...], while template marker syntax says [$rule_instruction] - this is consistent and correct
server.py is 580 lines - borderline but acceptable for a single-file backend

Jobs are stored in-memory (dict) and also persisted to MongoDB - if server restarts, in-memory jobs lost but DB has them. Download endpoint only checks in-memory jobs dict (not DB), so downloads fail after server restart. This is a potential bug.
fill_markers_with_ollama: individual fallback calls Ollama sequentially for each marker - could be slow for many markers but acceptable
No cleanup of old job files in /tmp/docfiller - disk accumulates over time
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend: all 12 tests pass. Browser automation (Playwright) crashes with SIGSEGV in headless Chromium - this is an environment-level issue. Frontend code reviewed manually: Step 1 has Ollama URL input (default http://localhost:11434), Test Connection button, Ollama Offline badge, warning box when disconnected, disabled Next button. Step indicator shows 3 steps. Step 2 has source/template dropzones. Step 3 has summary grid and process button. All data-testid attributes are present. One code issue: download endpoint only checks in-memory jobs dict, not MongoDB - downloads would fail after server restart.

rca_of_issues.download_after_restart: In /api/download/{job_id}/{fmt}, code only checks in-memory `jobs` dict. If server restarts, in-memory state is lost even though MongoDB has the job record. Fix: look up file paths from stored job or re-derive path from STORAGE_DIR/job_id/filled_document.docx
